logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF and iron deficiency (ferritin <100 mcg/L or 100-300 mcg/L with transferrin saturation <20%) with or without anemia, intravenous iron replacement is reasonable to improve functional status and quality of life. Oral iron is not adequate to treat iron deficiency in HF.

source_text: In patients with HFrEF and iron deficiency with or without anemia, intravenous iron replacement is reasonable to improve functional status and QOL.

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF and anemia, erythropoietin-stimulating agents (e.g., darbepoetin alfa) should not be used to improve morbidity and mortality. A randomized trial of darbepoetin alfa showed no benefit and increased thrombotic events including stroke.

source_text: In patients with HF and anemia, erythropoietin-stimulating agents should not be used to improve morbidity and mortality.

logic_node.action: Uptitrate GDMT to maximally tolerated target dose
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF and hypertension, uptitration of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) to the maximally tolerated target dose is recommended for blood pressure control. Hypertension represents an opportunity to maximize GDMT to goal blood pressures.

source_text: In patients with HFrEF and hypertension, uptitration of GDMT to the maximally tolerated target dose is recommended.

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF and suspicion of sleep-disordered breathing, a formal sleep assessment is reasonable to confirm the diagnosis and differentiate between obstructive and central sleep apnea. Decision to refer should be based on clinical judgment, as daytime sleepiness may not reflect the degree of underlying sleep-disordered breathing.

source_text: In patients with HF and suspicion of sleep-disordered breathing, a formal sleep assessment is reasonable to confirm the diagnosis and differentiate between obstructive and central sleep apnea.

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF and obstructive sleep apnea, continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) may be reasonable to improve sleep quality and decrease daytime sleepiness. CPAP has not been shown to affect survival but is associated with better sleep quality and nocturnal oxygenation.

source_text: In patients with HF and obstructive sleep apnea, continuous positive airway pressure may be reasonable to improve sleep quality and decrease daytime sleepiness.

logic_node.action_detail: In patients with NYHA class II to IV HFrEF and central sleep apnea, adaptive servo-ventilation causes harm. Two RCTs showed increased mortality with adaptive servo-ventilation in this population, supported by meta-analyses.

source_text: In patients with NYHA class II to IV HFrEF and central sleep apnea, adaptive servo-ventilation causes harm.

logic_node.action: Use SGLT2 inhibitor for hyperglycemia and HF outcomes
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF and type 2 diabetes, SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended as first-line agents for hyperglycemia management and to reduce HF-related morbidity and mortality. Two RCTs (DAPA-HF, EMPEROR-Reduced) in 8474 patients with NYHA II-IV and LVEF <=40% showed reductions in all-cause death (13%), CV death (14%), HF hospitalization (26%), and renal outcomes (38%).

source_text: In patients with HF and type 2 diabetes, the use of SGLT2i is recommended for the management of hyperglycemia and to reduce HF-related morbidity and mortality.

logic_node.action_detail: Patients on SGLT2 inhibitors should be closely monitored for potential risks including severe genitourinary infections and, less commonly, diabetic ketoacidosis.

source_text: Patients on SGLT2i should be closely monitored for potential risks, including severe genitourinary infections and, less commonly, diabetic ketoacidosis.

logic_node.action: Define iron deficiency criteria in HF
logic_node.action_detail: Iron deficiency in HF is defined as ferritin level <100 mcg/L, or ferritin 100-300 mcg/L with transferrin saturation <20%. Routine baseline assessment of all patients with HF includes evaluation for anemia. Iron deficiency is independently associated with reduced exercise capacity.

source_text: Iron deficiency is usually defined as ferritin level <100 mcg/L or 100 to 300 mcg/L, if the transferrin saturation is <20%.

logic_node.action: Do not use oral iron supplementation
logic_node.action_detail: Oral iron supplementation is not adequate to treat iron deficiency in patients with HF due to poor absorption and inadequacy to replete iron stores. The IRONOUT HF trial showed no improvement with oral iron supplementation. Intravenous iron is the appropriate route.

source_text: Oral iron is not adequate to treat iron deficiency anemia in patients with HF. This is attributed to the poor absorption of oral iron and inadequacy of oral iron to replete the iron stores.
